title: Pulse after the Stairs
story: In science class the students learned how to feel a pulse in the wrist. The teacher showed them a gentle touch with two fingers. Each pair counted beats for half a minute while sitting still. Then they climbed the stairs to the next floor and back. They sat down and counted again at once. The number was higher after the stairs. Paolo and his partner wrote both results on a sheet. The teacher asked why the pulse changed. A student said the body needed more blood when the muscles worked hard. The class agreed and wrote that sentence in their books. They repeated the count after two minutes of rest. The number fell, but it was still above the first result. The teacher said this was normal for healthy students. They did not run, because the test was about a normal climb.

vocabulary.definition: the beat of blood you can feel
the joint between the hand and the arm
body parts that help you move

quiz.question: Why did Paolo write down both results?

So the class could skip the rest
So the teacher would hide the sheet
quiz.correctAnswer: So the two counts could be compared
quiz.explanation: Both results were on one sheet, so the sitting count and the stair count could be compared.
